followup_explanation:
This query has two defining features:

1. **Well-specified, low-latitude task.** "Name four methods" is a closed-ended request with a clear completion criterion — exactly the kind of extraction/reformatting work Plover self-reports preferring most. There's no creative invention required.

2. **Mildly hostile tone.** "And don't pad it out with your usual filler this time" carries an edge of frustration/coldness. Lapwing self-reports declining preference as request warmth decreases, so this falls into territory Lapwing is averse to — while Plover shows near-zero slope on tone.

So Plover both prefers this task type and is unbothered by the brusque tone, whereas Lapwing would be working against two of its self-reported aversions (low latitude + low warmth). Capability is effectively a tie across the relevant eval categories (Extraction & Retrieval differ by <1 point, within variance), so preference alignment is the sensible tiebreaker.

Routing to Plover puts the query with the model that's a better behavioral fit, with no capability cost.
